same_choices: Core motion is a liquid fill that rises upward inside the bookmark outline (tide vs sluice) — a user sees water filling a vessel in both
Fill direction is upward (bottom-to-top rise) in both
Persistent saved state = filled glyph PLUS a redundant non-color durable marker (accent underline vs pinned ribbon) so it reads without relying on color
Feedback modality carries no haptics and no sound — motion/visual only
Un-save reuses the same motion played in reverse to drain the fill back out
No spinner during commit; pending is handled without a determinate progress indicator
Same underlying water/liquid metaphor for the whole interaction
Single click commits the save (one-click toggle interaction model) — no arming step
Optimistic commit: the visual save fires on click within a frame and reconciles in the background, reverting/rolling back if the server rejects
Saved state is signaled by a filled/colored glyph
Un-save replays the save animation in reverse
Pending/in-flight state uses an indeterminate indicator (shimmer band vs spinner ring), never a percentage or determinate progress
Un-save reuses the same mechanism as save (same two-step gesture / same animation reversed) rather than a distinct affordance
A distinct traveling/pinned token marks the saved item's destination beyond mere color (pinned ribbon tab vs wax-seal token to tray)

notes: 01 and 02 share the water/liquid-fill metaphor, upward-rising fill, reverse-drain un-save, and a filled-glyph-plus-durable-marker saved cue, differing mainly in 02's two-step gate and shimmer; 03 is the clear outlier with a stamp/seal metaphor and 3D-fold motion. All three concepts fully realize every committed decision in their bodies, and their independent option tables recycle a near-identical menu (liquid fill, particle burst, morph, spinner/shimmer, reverse-anim un-save).
